=== Alert / loud ===
something went wrong and the reader must be interrupted: assertive, with the tone said in words as well as drawn in colour
<div role="alert"><div><span aria-hidden="true"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></span><p><span>Error: </span>Deploy failed</p></div><p>The build exited 1 after 42 seconds.</p><div><button type="button">View logs</button></div><a aria-label="Dismiss deploy failure" data-fui-push-state="/apps?dismiss=1" data-fui-rpc="/island/alerts?dismiss=1" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="alerts" href="/apps?dismiss=1">×</a></div>

=== Alert / quiet ===
the default: a standing message that is on screen anyway and must not interrupt whatever is being read
<div><div><p>3 apps need attention</p></div></div>

=== Alert / already there ===
the confirmation after a post-and-redirect — present at load, so the only reliable way to announce it is to put the reader on it
<div autofocus="" id="restarted" tabindex="-1"><div><p>App restarted</p></div></div>

=== Badge / plain ===
a badge is a word, and the word is the accessible name — which is why the icon beside it is hidden rather than read twice
<span>running</span>

=== Badge / with an icon ===
the icon adds emphasis and no meaning: anything it means that the label does not say belongs in the label
<span><span aria-hidden="true"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></span>degraded</span>

=== Button / labelled ===
the ordinary case, and the reason type is always stated: inside a form the default is submit
<button type="button">Save changes</button>

=== Button / icon only ===
a button with no text still needs a name, or it cannot be operated by anyone who cannot see it
<button aria-label="Close" type="button"><span aria-hidden="true"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></span></button>

=== Button / link that looks like a button ===
it navigates, so it is an anchor — a button that changes the URL is a button a middle click cannot open
<a href="/docs">Read the docs</a>

=== Button / off-site link ===
a link that leaves the site opens a new tab and severs the opener — target=_blank without the noopener rel hands the destination a window handle back
<a href="https://example.com/docs" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Read the changelog</a>

=== Button / disabled link ===
a disabled anchor is not a thing in HTML, so the href goes and aria-disabled says why, rather than leaving a live link that looks dead
<a aria-disabled="true" role="link" tabindex="-1">Rollback</a>

=== Button / firing a request ===
the request a click makes is a prop on the button that fires it, in one reviewable place: the rpc triple lands through the Action seam and cannot arrive any other way, so a button that fires a request says so in its props
<button data-fui-rpc="/apps/api/restart" data-fui-rpc-method="POST" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" type="button">Restart api</button>

=== Button / mutating a local signal ===
a click that never leaves the browser is still what the button DOES, so it travels the same seam as a request: the mutation's attribute sits on the button beside its label, where a reviewer reads them together
<button data-fui-signal-inc="replicas" type="button">Add replica</button>

=== Card / titled ===
the common card: a heading, a line of context, a body
<div><div><h3>Deployments</h3><p>Last 24 hours</p></div><div><p>Nothing yet.</p></div></div>

=== Card / bare ===
no title and no description means no header — an empty header is a stripe of padding that reads as a mistake
<div><div><p>Body only.</p></div></div>

=== Card / footed ===
the footer is where the actions that apply to the whole card live
<div><div><h3>Restart policy</h3></div><div><p>On failure, up to 3 times.</p></div><div><button type="button">Save</button></div></div>

=== Choice / checkbox with a hint ===
the label WRAPS the control, so the hit area is the whole row and there is no for/id pair left to go stale
<label><input name="prune" type="checkbox" value="1"><span>Prune old images<span>Keeps the last three builds.</span></span></label>

=== Choice / radio ===
a real radio, so one arrow key moves through the set and the browser enforces that exactly one is chosen
<label><input name="policy" type="radio" value="always"><span>Always</span></label>

=== Cluster / default ===
a row of controls is what the component is for, and it wraps by default — a row that cannot wrap is a row that overflows a phone
<div><button type="button">Restart</button><button type="button">Stop</button><button type="button">View logs</button></div>

=== Cluster / gap and alignment ===
controls of different heights meet on their middles: the gap is a step on the same scale every other primitive uses and the alignment is named on its own axis
<div><button type="button">Save</button><button aria-label="Deployment settings" type="button"><span aria-hidden="true"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></span></button><button type="button">Cancel</button></div>

=== Cluster / space between ===
justify-between puts the destructive action at the far end from the safe one — the space is the skin's, not a spacer element somebody wedged between them
<div><button type="button">Save</button><button type="button">Delete app</button></div>

=== Color / swatch ===
a colour input is useless alone to anyone who cannot see it, so the hex value stays beside it as text that can be read and typed — inside a Field, so the value is a labelled setting and not a bare control
<div><label for="color-accent">Accent colour</label><div data-hui-affix="" data-hui-color=""><input aria-label="Pick accent" data-hui-affix-swatch="" id="color-accent-picker" tabindex="-1" type="color" value="#10b981"><input autocapitalize="off" autocomplete="off" data-hui-affix-input="" id="color-accent" name="accent" spellcheck="false" type="text" value="#10b981"></div></div>

=== ConditionalField / shown when the watched field matches ===
rendered visible with no hidden attribute, because a field only script can reveal is a field a scriptless reader never reaches — the runtime hides it when the watched field does not match, and not before
<label><input name="notify" type="radio" value="webhook"><span>Webhook</span></label><div data-hui-when="notify" data-hui-when-value="webhook"><div><label for="cond-webhook-url">Webhook URL</label><input id="cond-webhook-url" name="webhook-url" type="text"></div></div>

=== Container / reading measure ===
the default is the measure a page of prose reads at — line length is readability, decided here once so no page has to remember to ask for it
<div><p>One leader runs the cluster and any number of workers join it.</p></div>

=== Container / small ===
a focused task wants a short measure — a sign-in card, one setting — where a full-width line would wander
<div><p>Sign in to continue.</p></div>

=== Container / medium ===
a settings form sits between prose and dashboard: wide enough for label and field beside each other, narrow enough that the eye keeps the line
<div><p>HTTP port 80, HTTPS port 443.</p></div>

=== Container / large ===
the widest bounded measure — wide content such as a table of apps, still stopped somewhere so a line cannot run the width of the screen
<div><p>Eleven apps across three workers.</p></div>

=== Container / full ===
full drops the maximum and keeps the gutter — a dashboard should use the whole screen, and the gutter is the one thing it may not lose, because the edge of a phone is where text stops being readable
<div><p>CPU, memory and network for every node.</p></div>

=== Divider / horizontal ===
the default is a real hr: a break between two groups of content means separator, and the element already says it, so no role is claimed
<hr>

=== Divider / vertical ===
inside a row the break runs along the block axis, and aria-orientation says so — a vertical rule drawn as a bare line says nothing about which way the groups sit
<hr aria-orientation="vertical">

=== Divider / labelled ===
a label cannot live in an hr — it has no content model — so the separator role is claimed on the div that replaces it and the lines around the words are hidden
<div role="separator"><span aria-hidden="true"></span><span>or</span><span aria-hidden="true"></span></div>

=== Field / hinted ===
the hint is tied to the control by id, or it is on screen for sighted users only and the format rule never arrives
<div><label for="field-port">Port</label><input aria-describedby="field-port-hint" id="field-port" name="field-port" type="text"><p id="field-port-hint">1–65535</p></div>

=== Field / errored ===
the error JOINS the hint in the description, ahead of it: the hint is the rule the value must obey and the error is the violation, so dropping the rule exactly when it was broken is dropping it when it is needed most — and the correction is read first because it comes first
<div><label for="field-port-bad">Port</label><input aria-describedby="field-port-bad-error field-port-bad-hint" aria-invalid="true" id="field-port-bad" name="field-port-bad" type="text"><p id="field-port-bad-error" role="alert">Already in use.</p><p id="field-port-bad-hint">1–65535</p></div>

=== Field / reserved error node ===
a script that fills the error without re-rendering needs the node and its id already in the description — an empty described-by target announces nothing until it is filled, which is the point, and the stylesheet keeps the empty node out of the layout
<div><label for="field-token-live">Token</label><input aria-describedby="field-token-live-error" id="field-token-live" name="field-token-live" type="text"><p id="field-token-live-error" role="alert"></p></div>

=== Field / required ===
required is a state the parser is told about, not a red asterisk — which is a picture of a rule
<div><label data-required="" for="app">App name</label><input id="app" name="app" required="" type="text"></div>

=== FieldRow / pair ===
two fields side by side are still two fields: the row adds layout and no semantics, so nothing here is announced
<div><div><label for="from">From</label><input id="from" name="from" type="text"></div><div><label for="to">To</label><input id="to" name="to" type="text"></div></div>

=== FileUpload / with a hint ===
the zone is a label around a real input, so the whole target opens the picker — and the call to action is styled text, because a button inside a label swallows the label's click
<div data-hui-drop="" data-hui-drop-input="backup" data-hui-drop-many="{n} files selected: {names}." data-hui-drop-one="{name} selected."><label for="backup"><span>Drag an archive here, or </span><span>choose a file</span><span id="backup-accept">.tar.gz up to 2 GB</span></label><input accept=".tar.gz" aria-describedby="backup-accept" id="backup" name="backup" type="file"><ul data-hui-drop-list="" role="list"></ul><span data-hui-drop-status="" role="status"></span></div>

=== Form / a create form ===
the fields land in the body and the submits in the actions row, and the method defaults to post so a create never rides a GET a browser may repeat on its own
<form action="/apps" aria-label="Create an app" method="post"><div><div><label for="new-app-name">App name</label><input id="new-app-name" name="app-name" type="text"></div></div><div><button type="submit">Create app</button></div></form>

=== Form / after a failed submit ===
errors set the hook that moves focus to the summary, so a screen reader hears what went wrong instead of sitting on an unchanged-looking page
<form action="/apps" data-hui-form-errors="" method="post" novalidate=""><div aria-labelledby="form-dup-errors-title" id="form-dup-errors" role="alert" tabindex="-1"><h2 id="form-dup-errors-title">There is a problem</h2><ul><li><a href="#dup-app-name">That name is taken.</a></li></ul></div><div><div><label for="dup-app-name">App name</label><input aria-describedby="dup-app-name-error" aria-invalid="true" id="dup-app-name" name="app-name" type="text"><p id="dup-app-name-error" role="alert">That name is taken.</p></div></div><div><button type="submit">Create app</button></div></form>

=== Form / with a file upload ===
multipart sets the encoding a file input needs, because without it the browser submits the file's name and no contents, which looks like a server bug and is not one
<form action="/apps/definition" enctype="multipart/form-data" method="post"><div><div data-hui-drop="" data-hui-drop-input="definition-file" data-hui-drop-many="{n} files selected: {names}." data-hui-drop-one="{name} selected."><label for="definition-file"><span>Captain definition</span><span>Choose a file</span></label><input id="definition-file" name="definition" type="file"><ul data-hui-drop-list="" role="list"></ul><span data-hui-drop-status="" role="status"></span></div></div><div><button type="submit">Upload</button></div></form>

=== Grid / minimum column and gap ===
Min is a floor — a column never gets narrower than the named step before the grid gives one up — and the name is what keeps the floor wired: the framework's Grid took a free-form Min that nothing read, so every auto-fit grid was the default width whatever its author asked
<div><p>blog — 2 vCPU</p><p>wiki — 1 vCPU</p><p>api — 4 vCPU</p></div>

=== Group / radio set ===
the legend is the question the choices answer — without it a screen reader reads three labels and never says what is being decided
<fieldset><legend>Restart policy</legend><label><input name="policy" type="radio" value="always"><span>Always</span></label><label><input name="policy" type="radio" value="failure"><span>On failure</span></label></fieldset>

=== Group / required set ===
the cue and the rule are two different things: data-required on the legend is what a sighted reader looks for, and the required attribute on a leaf is what the browser enforces — a group carrying only one of them is a group that either lies or looks optional
<fieldset><legend data-required="">Plan</legend><label><input name="plan" required="" type="radio" value="free"><span>Free</span></label><label><input name="plan" type="radio" value="pro"><span>Pro</span></label></fieldset>

=== Input / described ===
the description it is handed is written out: six of the eight text controls once accepted DescribedBy and dropped it, so the field wired a relationship to an attribute nobody rendered — here the control sits in a Field the way a page would use it, and the hint arrives through that relationship
<div><label for="input-port">Port</label><input aria-describedby="input-port-hint" id="input-port" name="port" type="text" value="8080"><p id="input-port-hint">1–65535</p></div>

=== Input / invalid ===
aria-invalid is the state; the red border is the picture of it
<div><label for="input-port-bad">Port</label><input aria-describedby="input-port-bad-error" aria-invalid="true" id="input-port-bad" name="port" type="text"><p id="input-port-bad-error" role="alert">Already in use.</p></div>

=== InputGroup / an input with a button ===
with no label the group is a plain div, because wrapping labelled controls in a group with a third name makes a screen reader read the group name before each one
<div><div><label for="jump-app">Jump to app</label><input id="jump-app" name="app" type="text" value="registry app"><p id="jump-app-hint">Jump to an app in this cluster.</p></div><button type="submit">Go</button></div>

=== InputGroup / two focusable things ===
a group holding more than one focusable control takes a role and a name, so it appears in the landmark list as one identifiable control
<div aria-label="Webhook URL and port" role="group"><div><label for="hook-host">Host</label><input id="hook-host" name="host" type="text" value="app.example.com"></div><div><label for="hook-port">Port</label><input id="hook-port" name="port" type="text" value="30000"></div></div>

=== LightboxViewer / full ===
the working end of a gallery: nav, caption and download all on, so every hook, binding and button a module or a signal could lose is on the page
<div data-hui-lightbox="photos" data-hui-lightbox-nav="true"><figure><span data-fui-signal="alt" data-fui-signal-mode="text" id="photos-title">Image viewer</span><img data-fui-signal="src" data-fui-signal-attr="src" data-fui-signal-mode="attr" data-hui-lightbox-image=""><figcaption data-fui-signal="caption" data-fui-signal-mode="text"></figcaption></figure><div><button aria-label="Previous image" data-hui-lightbox-prev="photos" type="button"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></button><button aria-label="Next image" data-hui-lightbox-next="photos" type="button"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></button><a aria-label="Download image" data-fui-signal="src" data-fui-signal-attr="href" data-fui-signal-mode="attr" download=""><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></a></div></div>

=== LightboxViewer / bare ===
the minimum a viewer is: a named image and its accessible name, nothing optional — a markdown figure or a single inline photo needs no nav and saves the buttons
<div data-hui-lightbox="figure"><figure><span data-fui-signal="alt" data-fui-signal-mode="text" id="figure-title">Image viewer</span><img data-fui-signal="src" data-fui-signal-attr="src" data-fui-signal-mode="attr" data-hui-lightbox-image=""></figure></div>

=== LightboxViewer / framework wiring ===
the binder's spellings instead of the hooks: the same identity, nav opt-in, buttons and zoom target as data-fui-lightbox*, for the framework module a styled lightbox ships — the hui twins are suppressed here; they render exactly when the host's own module is the intended binder
<div data-fui-lightbox="photos" data-fui-lightbox-nav="true"><figure><span data-fui-signal="alt" data-fui-signal-mode="text" id="photos-title">Image viewer</span><img data-fui-lightbox-image="" data-fui-signal="src" data-fui-signal-attr="src" data-fui-signal-mode="attr"></figure><div><button aria-label="Previous image" data-fui-lightbox-prev="photos" type="button"></button><button aria-label="Next image" data-fui-lightbox-next="photos" type="button"></button><a aria-label="Download image" data-fui-signal="src" data-fui-signal-attr="href" data-fui-signal-mode="attr" download=""></a></div></div>

=== OptimisticAction / default ===
both labels ship in the SSR so the optimistic flip needs no round-trip, the method is absent because POST is the runtime's default, and the status span exists because the framework's shake announces nothing
<button data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/apps/blog/restart" data-hui-action-failed="Could not save. Try again." data-state="idle" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="">Restart now</span><span data-hui-action-done="" hidden="">Restarting</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== OptimisticAction / with icons ===
each label carries its own icon so the flip swaps glyph and word together, and both are aria-hidden because the words are the meaning — a check mark nobody can hear says nothing
<button data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/apps/blog/pin" data-hui-action-failed="Could not save. Try again." data-state="idle" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle=""><span aria-hidden="true"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></span>Pin</span><span data-hui-action-done="" hidden=""><span aria-hidden="true"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></span>Pinned</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== OptimisticAction / delete, not post ===
a method other than POST is published as an attribute, because the runtime defaults to POST and an unstated DELETE would fire the wrong request entirely
<button data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/webhooks/9" data-hui-action-failed="Could not save. Try again." data-hui-action-method="DELETE" data-state="idle" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="">Remove webhook</span><span data-hui-action-done="" hidden="">Removed</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== OptimisticAction / disabled ===
a disabled optimistic button still ships both labels and its announcement hook — disabling is a state of the click, not of the contract, and the runtime re-enables the button itself while a mutation is in flight
<button data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/apps/blog/redeploy" data-hui-action-failed="Could not save. Try again." data-state="idle" disabled="" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="">Redeploy</span><span data-hui-action-done="" hidden="">Redeploying</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== Pagination / middle of a long run ===
the gap is a span and not a link, the current page says aria-current=page rather than being told apart by weight, and a page change is an island update rather than a route: every anchor keeps its href for no script and carries the RPC contract beside it
<nav aria-label="Application pages, middle"><div><a data-fui-push-state="/apps?page=4" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?page=4" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?page=4">Previous</a><a data-fui-push-state="/apps?page=1" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?page=1" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?page=1">1</a><span aria-hidden="true">…</span><a data-fui-push-state="/apps?page=4" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?page=4" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?page=4">4</a><a aria-current="page" data-fui-push-state="/apps?page=5" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?page=5" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?page=5">5</a><a data-fui-push-state="/apps?page=6" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?page=6" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?page=6">6</a><span aria-hidden="true">…</span><a data-fui-push-state="/apps?page=12" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?page=12" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?page=12">12</a><a data-fui-push-state="/apps?page=6" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?page=6" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?page=6">Next</a></div></nav>

=== Pagination / at the first page ===
Previous stays visible and named with no href — removing it moves every other control one place left — and a disabled end carries no island contract, because a control that goes nowhere fires nothing
<nav aria-label="Application pages, first"><div><a aria-disabled="true" tabindex="-1">Previous</a><a aria-current="page" data-fui-push-state="/apps?page=1" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?page=1" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?page=1">1</a><a data-fui-push-state="/apps?page=2" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?page=2" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?page=2">2</a><a data-fui-push-state="/apps?page=3" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?page=3" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?page=3">3</a><a data-fui-push-state="/apps?page=2" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?page=2" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?page=2">Next</a></div></nav>

=== Password / revealable ===
the reveal button says what it will do next rather than what the field is doing now, and the labels it swaps between are published for the runtime instead of built from a class
<div><label for="password-token">Registry token</label><div data-hui-affix=""><input data-hui-affix-input="" id="password-token" name="token" type="password"><button aria-label="Show password" aria-pressed="false" data-hui-hide-label="Hide password" data-hui-hide-text="Hide" data-hui-reveal="" data-hui-show-label="Show password" data-hui-show-text="Show" type="button">Show</button></div></div>

=== Section / named ===
a name is what makes it a landmark, and the name comes from the heading itself rather than a second string that can drift from it
<section aria-labelledby="section-volumes-title"><div><div><h2 id="section-volumes-title">Volumes</h2><p>Disks attached to this node.</p></div><div><button type="button">Add</button></div></div><div><p>Two volumes.</p></div></section>

=== Section / unnamed ===
no title means a plain div: a section with no name is a row in the landmark list that says nothing, which is worse than not being in it
<div><div><p>Loose content.</p></div></div>

=== Section / deeper in the outline ===
the level is the caller's decision — a section under an h2 that renders an h2 leaves a hole a screen reader user has to guess at
<section aria-labelledby="section-mounts-title"><div><h3 id="section-mounts-title">Mounts</h3></div><div><p>One.</p></div></section>

=== Select / options ===
a real select, because the platform's own picker is the one thing that already works on a phone, with a keyboard, and under every screen reader
<select id="region" name="region"><option value="us-east">US East</option><option selected="" value="eu-west">EU West</option></select>

=== Skeleton / three lines ===
every bar is hidden from the tree: a screen reader reading out eight empty boxes, or announcing each shimmer, is strictly worse than one polite "Loading apps" and silence
<div data-hui-lines="3" role="status"><span aria-hidden="true"></span><span aria-hidden="true"></span><span aria-hidden="true" data-hui-skeleton-last=""></span><span>Loading apps</span></div>

=== Spacer / plain ===
it renders nothing, says nothing, and is in the markup only because a row needs a thing to grow — the space between two controls is the skin's, not a third control somebody wedged between them
<div><button type="button">Save</button><span aria-hidden="true" data-hui-grow="1"></span><button type="button">Delete app</button></div>

=== Spacer / bounded ===
a floor and a ceiling are names from the gap scale, so a spacer that must stay legible at any width says so in the same vocabulary every other gap uses
<div>Queued builds<span aria-hidden="true" data-hui-grow="2"></span>2</div>

=== Spacer / leader in a contents list ===
the dotted line between a term and its value is what ties the pair together once the row is wider than they are — and the spacer is a span so the list can be one paragraph, which a div would silently split
<p>Restarts<span aria-hidden="true" data-hui-grow="1"></span>263</p>

=== Spacer / rule ===
a hairline across the space reads as structure rather than as a tie, and the two are one knob each: a line that must be both is a line nobody chose
<p>Deploys today<span aria-hidden="true" data-hui-grow="1"></span>8</p>

=== Spinner / inline wait ===
role=status, not progressbar: a progressbar promises a value and a spinner has none — and the label says what is being waited for, because a moving shape says nothing on its own
<span><span aria-hidden="true"></span><span>Checking the registry</span></span>

=== Stack / default gap ===
no gap named is still a gap: the default is this primitive's own rhythm, so two pages that say nothing agree
<div><p>CPU is back under 60%.</p><p>The worker drained its deploy queue overnight.</p></div>

=== Stack / named gap ===
the step is a name from the scale, never a length the caller brings — the class either exists in the skin or the value is a typo, and both show the first time anyone looks
<div><p>Queued builds: 0.</p><p>Running builds: 2.</p></div>

=== Stack / one child ===
a stack of one is still a stack: the element is the seam the second block arrives into, and a wrapper that appears with it moves everything below
<div><p>No volumes are attached to this node.</p></div>

=== Steps / part way ===
a rail of states, not a set of controls: each step's data-state drives both its marker and the line drawn between markers, so the picture cannot disagree with the states
<ol><li data-state="done"><span>✓</span><span>Source</span></li><li aria-current="step" data-state="current"><span>2</span><span>Build</span></li><li data-state="todo"><span>3</span><span>Deploy</span></li></ol>

=== Steps / not started ===
zero is a real value — nothing has begun — and is not the same as being on the first step
<ol><li data-state="todo"><span>1</span><span>Source</span></li><li data-state="todo"><span>2</span><span>Build</span></li><li data-state="todo"><span>3</span><span>Deploy</span></li></ol>

=== Switch / on ===
a checkbox that says role=switch: it submits like a checkbox and is announced as on or off rather than checked or unchecked
<label><input checked="" name="auto" role="switch" type="checkbox"><span>Restart automatically</span></label>

=== SystemBanner / deploy in progress ===
a message about the system, shown by the server's own render: role=status so it waits its turn, one action, and the tone said in words as well as drawn in colour
<div data-hui-system="" data-hui-system-id="sys-deploy" role="status"><p><span>Information: </span>Deploy in progress</p><p>blog is moving to image 41; the app stays reachable the whole time.</p><div><button type="button">View the deploy</button></div><button aria-label="Dismiss: Deploy in progress" data-hui-system-dismiss="" type="button">×</button></div>

=== SystemBanner / offline ===
the built-in connection message, and the one system banner worth interrupting for: assertive, marked as the runtime's, shipped hidden because the runtime — not the page — shows it, and carrying no dismiss because its ending is the reconnect
<div aria-live="assertive" data-hui-system="" data-hui-system-id="sys-offline" data-hui-system-offline="" hidden="" role="alert"><p><span>Warning: </span>Connection lost</p><p>Changes are paused until the connection comes back.</p></div>

=== SystemBanner / new version ===
a dismissable message the page did not show: it ships hidden for an island swap or the runtime to reveal, and the id is what keeps it from being shown twice
<div data-hui-system="" data-hui-system-id="sys-version" hidden="" role="status"><p><span>Success: </span>A new version is ready</p><p>Reload to pick up version 0.4.2.</p><button aria-label="Dismiss: A new version is ready" data-hui-system-dismiss="" type="button">×</button></div>

=== SystemBanner / maintenance, and the version is old ===
the danger tone said as a word before the title, and two banners at once to prove the ids keep them from doubling up
<div data-hui-system="" data-hui-system-id="sys-maint" role="status"><p><span>Error: </span>Ending in 4 minutes</p><p>This control plane restarts at 20:00 UTC.</p><button aria-label="Dismiss: Ending in 4 minutes" data-hui-system-dismiss="" type="button">×</button></div><div data-hui-system="" data-hui-system-id="sys-old" hidden="" role="status"><p><span>Information: </span>This browser is not supported</p><button aria-label="Dismiss: This browser is not supported" data-hui-system-dismiss="" type="button">×</button></div>

=== Table / sorted, carrying a query, one header-less sortable column ===
aria-sort on the active column and none on the rest, the href's sort and dir replaced rather than appended so the query the screen carries survives a sort, and the header-less column's anchor named from Strings — an anchor with no text is a control with no name
<div><div aria-labelledby="table-applications-caption" role="region" tabindex="0"><table role="table"><caption id="table-applications-caption">Applications</caption><thead role="rowgroup"><tr role="row"><th aria-sort="ascending" role="columnheader" scope="col"><a href="/apps?dir=desc&amp;page=3&amp;q=blog&amp;sort=name">Name</a></th><th aria-sort="none" role="columnheader" scope="col"><a aria-label="Sort by env" href="/apps?dir=asc&amp;page=3&amp;q=blog&amp;sort=env"></a></th><th role="columnheader" scope="col">Region</th></tr></thead><tbody role="rowgroup"><tr id="app-1" role="row"><td data-label="Name" role="cell">blog</td><td role="cell">production</td><td data-label="Region" role="cell">eu-1</td></tr><tr id="app-2" role="row"><td data-label="Name" role="cell">shop</td><td role="cell">staging</td><td data-label="Region" role="cell">us-1</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>

=== Table / the same table as an island ===
an embedded table's sort anchors carry the RPC contract beside their hrefs — the page without script, the region update with it, the query shared so the two answer one question — and the endpoint that carries its own query joins rather than stacks a second one
<div><div role="region" tabindex="0"><table role="table"><thead role="rowgroup"><tr role="row"><th aria-sort="none" role="columnheader" scope="col"><a data-fui-push-state="/apps?dir=asc&amp;q=blog&amp;sort=name" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?dir=asc&amp;keep=1&amp;q=blog&amp;sort=name" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?dir=asc&amp;q=blog&amp;sort=name">Name</a></th><th aria-sort="descending" role="columnheader" scope="col"><a data-fui-push-state="/apps?dir=asc&amp;q=blog&amp;sort=env" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?dir=asc&amp;keep=1&amp;q=blog&amp;sort=env" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?dir=asc&amp;q=blog&amp;sort=env">Environment</a></th></tr></thead><tbody role="rowgroup"><tr id="app-1" role="row"><td data-label="Name" role="cell">blog</td><td data-label="Environment" role="cell">production</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>

=== Table / empty with a slot ===
an empty result still has named columns and usable sort controls — the head stays — and the one cell that spans them says what the caller means by nothing here, in the caller's words
<div><div aria-labelledby="table-applications-caption" role="region" tabindex="0"><table role="table"><caption id="table-applications-caption">Applications</caption><thead role="rowgroup"><tr role="row"><th aria-sort="none" role="columnheader" scope="col"><a href="/apps?dir=asc&amp;sort=name">Name</a></th><th role="columnheader" scope="col">Environment</th></tr></thead><tbody role="rowgroup"><tr role="row"><td colspan="2" role="cell"><p>No applications match.</p></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>

=== Table / with a footer ===
the footer renders as the scroll region's sibling, not inside the table, so a pager's nav landmark never nests in one — and the region is on the page with and without it, focusable either way
<div><div aria-labelledby="table-deployments-caption" role="region" tabindex="0"><table role="table"><caption id="table-deployments-caption">Deployments</caption><thead role="rowgroup"><tr role="row"><th role="columnheader" scope="col">Application</th><th role="columnheader" scope="col">Deployed</th></tr></thead><tbody role="rowgroup"><tr role="row"><td data-label="Application" role="cell">blog</td><td data-label="Deployed" role="cell">2 minutes ago</td></tr></tbody></table></div><nav aria-label="Deployment pages">Page 1 of 2</nav></div>

=== Table / bare, nothing to click ===
a read-only table is still a table: the caption is its name, the roles and scope are all that assistive technology is given, the header-less actions column is hidden rather than announced empty, and the scroll region is focusable even though this table has nothing to click — overflow is the viewport's decision, not the caller's
<div><div aria-labelledby="table-recent-deployments-caption" role="region" tabindex="0"><table role="table"><caption id="table-recent-deployments-caption">Recent deployments</caption><thead role="rowgroup"><tr role="row"><th role="columnheader" scope="col">Application</th><th role="columnheader" scope="col">Status</th><th aria-hidden="true" role="columnheader" scope="col"></th></tr></thead><tbody role="rowgroup"><tr role="row"><td data-label="Application" role="cell">blog</td><td data-label="Status" role="cell">healthy</td><td role="cell">View</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>

=== Tag / removable ===
the × names what it removes — twelve controls all called Remove tell a screen reader user nothing — and it is an anchor that keeps its href for no script while carrying the island contract, because dropping a filter is an in-page state change and never a route
<span>env=prod<a aria-label="Remove env=prod" data-fui-push-state="/apps?env=" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?env=" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?env=">×</a></span>

=== Tag / fixed ===
a tag with nothing to navigate to renders no control at all rather than a dead ×, and its icon is hidden from assistive technology exactly as a badge's is, because a tag is a badge with a dismiss control and the two must not drift
<span><span aria-hidden="true"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></span>leader</span>

=== Textarea / with content ===
the value is the element's text, not an attribute — which is why it is the one control whose content must be escaped rather than quoted
<textarea id="notes" name="notes">Restarted after the 4am alert.</textarea>

=== Textarea / growing ===
autogrow is the one core-runtime hook a control here renders — the behaviour belongs to the control, and the prop is the only seam that survives the prefix refusal
<div><label for="notes-grow">Release notes</label><textarea data-fui-autogrow="" id="notes-grow" name="notes">Grows to fit whatever is typed.</textarea></div>

=== Timeline / history ===
an event with no tone is the ordinary case and draws an untinted marker; ordered, because the order is the content: a screen reader announces the count and the position, so "3 of 7" locates you in the history without seeing the line down the left
<ol aria-label="Deploy history"><li><span aria-hidden="true"></span><div><time datetime="2026-09-08T11:04:00Z">3 days ago</time><p>Deployed</p><p>From main, by Donald.</p></div></li><li><span aria-hidden="true"></span><div><time datetime="2026-09-07T09:12:00Z">4 days ago</time><p>Build failed</p><p>Exit 1 in the test stage.</p></div></li><li><span aria-hidden="true"></span><div><time datetime="2026-09-06T16:40:00Z">5 days ago</time><p>Configuration changed</p></div></li></ol>

=== ToggleAction / idle ===
aria-pressed false and the committed span hidden: first paint matches the server's answer, and the runtime only ever flips what is already there
<button aria-pressed="false" data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/apps/blog/watch" data-hui-action-failed="Could not save. Try again." data-state="idle" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="">Watch</span><span data-hui-action-done="" hidden="">Watching</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== ToggleAction / committed at load ===
the server knows: aria-pressed is true and it is the idle span that is hidden, so a page that loads already-watching does not flash through the wrong label first — and each label carries its own aria-hidden icon, so the flip swaps glyph and word together
<button aria-pressed="true" data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/apps/blog/watch" data-hui-action-failed="Could not save. Try again." data-state="committed" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="" hidden=""><span aria-hidden="true"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></span>Watch</span><span data-hui-action-done=""><span aria-hidden="true"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></span>Watching</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== ToggleAction / unwatch, not post ===
a method other than POST is published as an attribute, because the primitive defaults to POST and an unstated DELETE would fire the wrong request entirely — the same rule the optimistic button's delete case states
<button aria-pressed="true" data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/apps/blog/watch" data-hui-action-failed="Could not save. Try again." data-hui-action-method="DELETE" data-state="committed" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="" hidden="">Watch</span><span data-hui-action-done="">Watching</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== ToggleAction / two in a mutex group ===
committing one member of a group revokes the other with no second request, so a plan picker reads as one choice rather than three independent buttons that can all be on
<button aria-pressed="true" data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/plan/starter" data-hui-action-failed="Could not save. Try again." data-hui-action-group="plan" data-state="committed" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="" hidden="">Starter</span><span data-hui-action-done="">Starter ✓</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button><button aria-pressed="false" data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/plan/pro" data-hui-action-failed="Could not save. Try again." data-hui-action-group="plan" data-state="idle" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="">Pro</span><span data-hui-action-done="" hidden="">Pro ✓</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== ToggleAction / untoggle, with its own endpoint ===
a committed button that can be clicked again publishes the untoggle endpoint and ships committed — the only state from which untoggle is reachable — so the revert is a request the server can refuse, not just a local flip
<button aria-pressed="true" data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/plan/pro" data-hui-action-failed="Could not save. Try again." data-hui-action-untoggle="/plan/none" data-state="committed" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="" hidden="">Pro</span><span data-hui-action-done="">Pro ✓</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== Toolbar / controls in a row ===
no role=toolbar: that role promises arrow-key roving with a single tab stop, and a promise a script-free component cannot keep is worse than saying nothing
<div><button type="button">New app</button><button type="button">Refresh</button></div>

=== ToolbarGroup / labelled group ===
the label names what the group of controls acts on, so the controls inside can stay short without becoming ambiguous
<div><span>Sort</span><button type="button">Name</button></div>

=== ToolbarSearch / search slot ===
the search field is the one control in a toolbar that should grow, so its wrapper is the GET form that submits it — an island update with script, the page's own query without
<form data-fui-rpc="/island/apps" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" method="get"><input aria-label="Search apps" name="q" type="search"></form>

=== ToolbarSpacer / gap ===
an empty element that pushes what follows to the far end — it renders nothing, says nothing, and is in the markup only because the layout needs a thing to grow
<div></div>

=== ValidationSummary / after a failed submit ===
it interrupts and can take focus, and every error is a link to the field it is about — a list of complaints you cannot navigate to is a list you have to hunt through
<div aria-labelledby="errors-title" id="errors" role="alert" tabindex="-1"><h2 id="errors-title">This form could not be saved</h2><ul><li><a href="#name">Enter an app name.</a></li><li><a href="#port">Port 8080 is already in use.</a></li></ul></div>

=== ValidationSummary / an error with no field ===
"the registry rejected the push" belongs to no input, and dropping it because it has nowhere to link would lose the only message that explains the failure
<div aria-labelledby="errors2-title" id="errors2" role="alert" tabindex="-1"><h2 id="errors2-title">This form could not be saved</h2><ul><li>The registry rejected the push.</li></ul></div>

=== ValidationSummary / nothing wrong ===
no errors renders nothing at all, so a page can ask for the summary unconditionally and not get an empty red box on first load
<p>Nothing to report.</p>

=== ValidationSummary / two summaries on one page ===
two forms that failed on one page label two summaries, and the required ids are what keep the titles from sharing one name — the reference gate reads both labels and both resolve to their own heading
<div aria-labelledby="errors-left-title" id="errors-left" role="alert" tabindex="-1"><h2 id="errors-left-title">There is a problem</h2><ul><li><a href="#left-name">Enter a name.</a></li></ul></div><div aria-labelledby="errors-right-title" id="errors-right" role="alert" tabindex="-1"><h2 id="errors-right-title">There is a problem</h2><ul><li><a href="#right-name">Enter a name.</a></li></ul></div>
